name: Treaty of Kalisz
summary: Casimir III of Poland and the Teutonic Order settle the long-running war over Pomerelia and Kuyavia: Poland recovers Kuyavia and Dobrzyń but cedes Pomerelia (including Danzig/Gdańsk) to the Order. Casimir uses the breathing space to focus on Galicia and internal reforms.

_quarry.structural_significance: Loss of Pomerelia leaves Poland landlocked on the Baltic until the Second Peace of Toruń (1466). Casimir's pivot to the south-east (annexation of Halych-Volhynia by 1349) sets the eastern expansion trajectory of the late medieval Polish state.
